top3.headline: GPT-6.2 Astra nears Claude Fable 5.2 at a third the price
top3.whyItMatters: When quality is close, price and speed decide which model your teams should use.

top3.headline: OpenAI's new models lead on cybersecurity, says Vercel's Rauch
top3.whyItMatters: Models this capable at security work raise the bar for every company's defenses.

top3.headline: T3 Code burned 31.7 trillion tokens in a single day
top3.whyItMatters: Agent coding is now a major cost line, so leaders need token budgets and tracking.

items.title: Theo: passing secrets to agents is now a top T3 Code feature
items.takeaway: Theo says passing secrets to agents in T3 Code began as a small feature; he now uses it several times a day.
items.soWhat: Agents need safe access to keys, so secret handling is becoming core agent tooling.

items.title: Meng To lists UI design skills that give coding agents taste
items.takeaway: His list includes Impeccable, which critiques, audits and polishes against generic UI, plus Emil Kowalski's UI and animation skills.
items.soWhat: Packaged design skills can lift agent-built interfaces above generic defaults.

items.title: Vitalik Buterin: investing beyond housing eases pressure for pricey homes
items.takeaway: He argues that when younger generations invest in stocks and digital assets instead of housing, the perverse incentives to keep housing expensive weaken.
items.soWhat: Where a generation keeps its savings shapes which housing policies it pushes for.

items.title: Theo: Opus 5.5 is still the best value for long coding runs
items.takeaway: Artificial Analysis no longer places Opus 5.5 on its value line; Theo disagrees for long-running coding and wants behavioral benchmarks.
items.soWhat: Leaderboards miss long-task behavior, so test models on your own long workflows.

items.title: Nvidia's board dispute becomes a lesson in board design
items.takeaway: Garry Tan: 'Only three people to remove from the board? Easy work. 15% shareholder vote coming.' Beff Jezos calls it a big lesson in board composition for founders.
items.soWhat: Who sits on the board decides who holds control when a company hits a crisis.

items.title: Satya Nadella opens Ignite on building a frontier AI ecosystem
items.takeaway: Satya Nadella posted highlights from his Ignite keynote opening on building a frontier ecosystem to turn AI advances into real-world impact.
items.soWhat: Microsoft frames AI as an ecosystem play, which shapes what reaches its enterprise customers.

items.title: T3 Code processed 31.7 trillion tokens in one day
items.takeaway: Theo says T3 Code hit 31.7 trillion tokens in a day, over $10M in API spend in 24 hours, and Claude's usage share held after OpenAI's release.
items.soWhat: Coding agents now drive real model spend, so token budgets belong in planning.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra nears Claude Fable 5.2 at a third the price
items.takeaway: On Alex Finn's benchmark Astra scored 312.7/500, 0.3 behind Fable 5.2, in a third of the time and a quarter of the tokens. Theo says it improved but is 'directionally, very bad'; swyx sees a solid minor upgrade.
items.soWhat: When quality is this close, model choice becomes a cost decision, so test on your own tasks.

items.title: Claude Desktop adds a Latest channel for more frequent builds
items.takeaway: On Windows and Mac, pick Latest in Settings > Desktop app; Stable stays the default and Latest can be less reliable.
items.soWhat: Teams can trial new Claude features early while most staff stay on Stable.

items.title: Rauch: OpenAI's new models lead on cybersecurity skill
items.takeaway: Guillermo Rauch calls OpenAI's new release the most cybersecurity-capable models in the world and points to Vercel's DeepsecBench, built on codebases no lab could train on.
items.soWhat: Models this good at security cut both ways, so review your exposure before attackers do.

items.title: Claude Code tests Code Mode: agents write scripts that chain tools
items.takeaway: Claude writes scripts that chain tools and can answer while long commands run. Opt in with an env flag.
items.soWhat: Agents that orchestrate your tools themselves make clean, scriptable internal tools more valuable.

items.title: a16z backs First Person Labs to build agents that know you
items.takeaway: a16z invests in First Person Labs, arguing personal agents need a deep, sensitive model of each user.
items.soWhat: Personal agents run on intimate data, so trust and privacy become the product.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, pitched as token-efficient
items.takeaway: OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are now available; Sam Altman calls them very token-efficient.
items.soWhat: Cheaper tokens per task change the math on which workflows are worth automating now.

items.title: Gemini Tasks expands free to hundreds of millions in six countries
items.takeaway: Sundar Pichai says Tasks in Gemini, powered by Gemini 4 Hydrogen, is expanding free of charge to hundreds of millions of people in six countries to hand off everyday life admin.
items.soWhat: Consumers will soon expect agents that finish chores, and your customers will bring that expectation.

items.title: Meng To builds a walkable Shinjuku night scene in one HTML file
items.takeaway: Meng To built a Shinjuku night-scene 3D site in three.js: one HTML file, no 3D models, all built in code, walkable with WASD, with time of day and seasons.
items.soWhat: Rich 3D experiences now fit in a single file, so small teams can try immersive ideas cheaply.

items.title: Nathan Benaich: AltaAres wins most lots in NATO counter-drone framework
items.takeaway: Nathan Benaich says AltaAres won six of 16 lots in NATO's counter-drone framework, more than any other supplier, so allied countries can buy its systems without another tender. He believes the team can build a global leader in autonomous defense.
items.soWhat: Early backers see autonomous defense as a real market, with procurement doors now opening.

items.title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5B to speed up AI drug design
items.takeaway: Demis Hassabis announces $5B in funding for Isomorphic Labs to accelerate AI drug design and its mission to 'Solve All Disease'.
items.soWhat: Capital is flowing to AI that does science, not chat, so watch your sector's research pipeline.

items.title: Simon Willison: run agents locally, execute their code in a sandbox
items.takeaway: Simon Willison describes an 'external sandbox' pattern: the coding agent runs on your Mac but executes code in a WebAssembly, QEMU or Apple Container sandbox. He shows demos for Claude Code and Codex.
items.soWhat: Sandboxed execution lets teams say yes to coding agents without handing over the whole machine.

items.title: Claude Code team: let agents verify their own work
items.takeaway: ClaudeDevs says Claude writes better code when it can verify its work, and that tests, benchmarks and end-to-end runs are now cheap. The team published how it thinks about verification.
items.soWhat: Agent output gets more reliable when checks are built in, so budget for tests, not reviews.

items.title: California's attorney general sues OpenAI over AI safeguards
items.takeaway: California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI, alleging it built AI models without the safeguards and monitoring needed to protect people, NBC News reports.
items.soWhat: Safeguards and monitoring are becoming legal questions, so document yours before regulators ask.

items.title: Tavi Costa: the US-China yield gap is the key macro divergence
items.takeaway: He shares a chart of US and China 10-year yields and calls the gap the most important divergence between two superpowers funding an AI arms race.
items.soWhat: Borrowing costs shape how long each superpower can keep funding its AI build-out.

voices.quote: Only three people to remove from the board? Easy work. 15% shareholder vote coming.
These models can do amazing things and are very token-efficient; we hope people will get great value from them.
Claude writes scripts that chain your tools together in sophisticated ways, and it can answer you while long commands are still running.
For personal agents to become useful in everyday life, they need a total understanding of you.
If GPT-6.2 Astra acted more like Muse Wonder Full, it would be a great model.
